problems.title: Substitute before taking the absolute value
problems.question: If $f(x)=|x+5|$, find $f(a^2-2)$.
problems.idea: Replace every x in the rule with the entire input.
formulas: For real a, a²≥0, so a²+3>0.
steps: The quantity inside is positive for every real a.
Its absolute value is therefore a²+3.

problems.title: Distance from a coordinate axis
problems.question: C(3m-1,2m+1) is in the third quadrant and is 8 units from the y-axis. Find m.
problems.idea: In the third quadrant both coordinates are negative.
formulas: Distance to the y-axis=|x|.
steps: Check the other coordinate: 2m+1=-11/3<0, so the third-quadrant condition holds.

problems.title: A line from its intercepts
problems.question: Find the line through E(0,-7) and F(2,0).
problems.idea: Compute its slope and read off the vertical intercept.
formulas: Slope=(y₂-y₁)/(x₂-x₁); y=mx+b.

problems.title: A parallel line through a point
problems.question: A line through the origin has x=3y at a nonzero point Q. Find the parallel line through K(-9,9).
problems.idea: Convert the coordinate relation into a slope.
formulas: Parallel nonvertical lines have equal slopes; y=mx+b.
steps: From x=3y, the original line is y=x/3.

problems.title: Which quadrants does a line enter?
problems.question: In which quadrants does y=-2x+3 lie?
problems.idea: Check the signs of x and y on the intervals separated by the intercepts.
formulas: Quadrants I,II,III,IV correspond to (+,+),(-,+),(-,-),(+,-).
steps: A negative x never gives a negative y, so quadrant III is absent.

problems.title: Maximum and minimum of a decreasing line
problems.question: Find the greatest and least values of y=-x-5 on [-1,3].
problems.idea: A negative slope means the function decreases as x increases.
formulas: For decreasing f on [a,b], maximum=f(a), minimum=f(b).
steps: At the left endpoint x=-1, y=1-5=-4.
At the right endpoint x=3, y=-3-5=-8.
All intermediate values lie between these.

problems.title: Use a known root to find a parameter
problems.question: One solution of $(2x-1)^2=b-4$ is x=-1. Find b.
problems.idea: Substitute the known solution.
formulas: If x is a solution, substitution makes the equation true.
steps: At x=-1, the squared quantity is (-3)²=9.

problems.title: Reflect across a descending diagonal
problems.question: Reflect M(-m,n) in the line y=-x.
problems.idea: Reflection swaps the coordinates and changes both signs.
formulas: Reflection in y=-x maps (x,y) to (-y,-x).
steps: For x=-m and y=n, the new first coordinate is -n.

problems.title: Find a line through two points
problems.question: Find the equation of the line through A(1,-1) and B(3,5).
problems.idea: Use the slope, then substitute either point.
formulas: m=(y₂-y₁)/(x₂-x₁); y=mx+b.
steps: The line is y=3x-4; B gives 5=9-4, confirming it.

problems.title: Clear denominators of a linear equation
problems.question: Solve $7-x-\frac{4x+6}{9}=6-\frac{15x+3}{12}$.
problems.idea: Multiply by the least common denominator 36.
formulas: Equivalent equations result from multiplying all terms by a nonzero number.

problems.title: An integer quotient restricts a parameter
problems.question: How many integers a make ax=x+9 have an integer solution x?
problems.idea: Solve for x and count divisors of 9.
formulas: (a-1)x=9; an integer quotient 9/d requires integer d to divide 9.
steps: a=1 gives 0=9 and fails. For a≠1, x=9/(a-1).

problems.title: A rectangle symmetric in both coordinate axes
problems.question: The x- and y-axes are symmetry axes of rectangle ABCD. A=(-3.1,2.3). Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Reflection in the axes gives all four vertices.
formulas: Rectangle perimeter=2(width+height).
steps: The width is 6.2 and the height is 4.6.

problems.title: Use a difference of squares to find two roots
problems.question: Find the product of the roots of $4(x-3)^2-9(2x+1)^2=0$.
problems.idea: Factor into two linear expressions.
steps: The roots are -9/4 and 3/8, whose product is -27/32.

problems.title: Translate a line left and upward
problems.question: Translate y=2x-5 by (x,y)↦(x-3,y+1). Find the image line.
problems.idea: Express the old coordinates through the new coordinates.
formulas: For translation (h,k), substitute x=X-h,y=Y-k into the original equation.
steps: Here X=x-3 and Y=y+1, so x=X+3,y=Y-1.

problems.title: Equal distances from the x-axis
problems.question: A(p,3) and B(5,p-1) are equally far from the x-axis, and B is in quadrant IV. Find p.
problems.idea: Use the absolute values of the vertical coordinates and then the quadrant condition.
formulas: Distance to the x-axis=|y|; quadrant IV requires x>0,y<0.
steps: The equal distances give |p-1|=3, so p=4 or p=-2.
Since B has negative y, p-1<0.

problems.title: Check whether the stated chords can exist
problems.question: Two perpendicular chords are divided at their intersection into lengths 2,4 and 3,5. Find the sum of their distances from the circle centre.
problems.idea: Check the intersecting-chords theorem before using midpoint distances.
formulas: Intersecting chords satisfy PA·PB=PC·PD; a circle centre lies on each chord’s perpendicular bisector.
steps: The products would be 2·4=8 and 3·5=15. They are unequal.
Therefore no circle can have these four chord segments.
The intended midpoint calculation gives |4-2|/2+|5-3|/2=2, but it overlooks the incompatible chord products.
problems.answer: No such circle exists; 2 is the apparent intended formal result.
problems.note: The printed lengths violate the intersecting-chords theorem, so the intended numerical choice is not a valid circle configuration.

problems.title: An inradius and a hypotenuse median
problems.question: A right triangle has median 5 cm from the right angle and inradius 1 cm. Find the sum of its legs.
problems.idea: The median gives the hypotenuse; the inradius then gives the leg sum.
formulas: Median to hypotenuse=c/2; right-triangle inradius r=(a+b-c)/2.

problems.title: Three tangent circles give an equilateral centre triangle
problems.question: Two equal small circles touch each other and internally touch a larger circle. One angle of their centre triangle is 60°. Find small radius/large radius.
problems.idea: The two equal centre distances make the triangle isosceles; a 60° angle makes it equilateral.
formulas: Internal tangency distance=R-r; external tangency distance=2r.
steps: The centre triangle has sides R-r,R-r,2r.
An isosceles triangle with any angle 60° has all angles 60°, so all sides are equal.

problems.title: Angles from the arcs between incircle contacts
problems.question: The incircle’s three contact points divide it into arcs in ratio 2:3:4. Find the triangle’s largest angle.
problems.idea: The angle between two tangents is supplementary to the minor arc between their contact points.
formulas: Arc angles total 360°; vertex angle=180°-contact arc.
steps: The 9 ratio units each measure 360°/9=40°. The arcs are 80°,120°,160°.

problems.title: Equal tangent segments in an isosceles triangle
problems.question: The incircle divides an equal side in ratio 3:4 measured from the apex. The perimeter is 44 cm. Find the base.
problems.idea: Tangent segments drawn from the same vertex have equal lengths.
formulas: From one external point, the two tangent segments to a circle are equal.
steps: Let the apex tangent length be 3t and each base-vertex tangent length be 4t.
Each equal side is 7t and the base is 8t.

problems.title: Equal halves of a circular track
problems.question: A cyclist moves uniformly on a circular track. Two photographers stand at different points of the track. The cyclist is closer to the second for 3 minutes between periods closer to the first. Find the lap time.
problems.idea: The perpendicular bisector of the photographers’ chord cuts the track into equal semicircles.
formulas: A chord’s perpendicular bisector passes through the circle centre.
steps: Points closer to either photographer lie on opposite sides of that perpendicular bisector.
Each photographer is nearer over exactly one semicircle.
At constant speed, 3 minutes for half a lap means 6 minutes for a whole lap.

problems.title: An exterior angle between two secants
problems.question: Two secants form an outside angle A equal to their smaller intercepted arc. The other two arcs outside the angle total 160°. Find A.
problems.idea: Combine the total arc measure with the outside-secant angle theorem.
formulas: Exterior secant angle=(far arc-near arc)/2; all arcs sum to 360°.
steps: Write the near arc as x; the angle is also x.
The far arc plus x is 360°-160°=200°, so far arc=200°-x.

problems.title: Use the remainder theorem
problems.question: Find the remainder when $3x^4-9x^3+7x-3$ is divided by x+1.
problems.idea: Evaluate the polynomial where the divisor is zero.
formulas: The remainder on division by x-a is P(a).

problems.title: The acute angle between two chords
problems.question: A,B,C,D lie successively on a circle. BAD=60°, ADB=38°, BDC=37°. Find the acute angle between AC and BD.
problems.idea: Use inscribed angles to recover the arcs opposite the chord-intersection angle.
formulas: Inscribed angle=half its intercepted arc; intersecting-chord angle=half the sum of opposite arcs.
steps: Angle BAD intercepts arc BCD=120°, so arc CD=120°-74°=46°.
One angle between AC and BD equals (arc AB+arc CD)/2=(76°+46°)/2=61°.
Its supplement is 119°, so the acute angle is 61°.

problems.title: A cyclic quadrilateral involving the incenter
problems.question: AA₁ and BB₁ are internal bisectors meeting at K. A₁,C,B₁,K are concyclic. Find angle KA₁B₁.
problems.idea: Use opposite cyclic angles to find C, then an inscribed angle.
formulas: Incenter angle AKB=90°+C/2; opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°.
steps: Because KA₁ and KB₁ point opposite KA and KB, angle A₁KB₁=90°+C/2.
Its opposite cyclic angle is A₁CB₁=C. Hence C+90°+C/2=180°, giving C=60°.
Angles KA₁B₁ and KCB₁ subtend the same chord KB₁.
